page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The processor includes 54 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for cryptographic acceleration and vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The system is provisioned with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

For I/O, the instance comes bundled with 237 GB of dedicated local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing high-throughput local disk access without consuming external volume bandwidth. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. The instance does not include a hardware GPU accelerator, focusing system resources entirely on CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and local storage I/O.

In synthetic benchmarks, the m6idn.xlarge posts midrange results for single-threaded tasks, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1601.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1892.08. Conversely, multithreaded capacity reflects the modest core count, registering bottom-quartile metrics across multithreaded stress-ng (3862.58), PassMark CPU score (5883.55), and multithreaded bzip3 decompression (19.62 GB/sec). Memory throughput reaches 30.03 GB/sec uncached sequential read and 25.36 GB/sec write.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high IOPS per dollar without additional EBS volume expenses, though overall multithreaded density is limited relative to larger instance sizes. The hardware profile is best aligned with general web serving, intermediate caching layers like Redis, transient data processing pipelines, and localized databases that benefit from low-latency scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual server offering 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. The configuration integrates 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage without GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmark results place single-threaded CPU tasks and memory throughput in the middle performance tiers, while multi-core computational throughput is constrained by the 4-vCPU footprint. The local NVMe disk provides substantial I/O throughput benefits compared to standard network-attached storage instances. The m6idn.xlarge is well suited for balanced enterprise workloads requiring fast local temporary storage, such as database caching, web application serving, continuous integration tasks, and intermediate batch data processing.
